description: Run several SQL statements (a migration, a seed, any script) against a registered foreign Postgres connection in ONE transaction, each statement inside its own savepoint. on_error='rollback' (default) rolls the whole script back at the first failure and reports external_pg.script_statement_failed naming the statement's number, keyword and text; on_error='continue' rolls back only the failing statement and commits the rest; commit=false runs everything then rolls back (a dry run). Statements are split by a dollar-quote and comment aware parser, so function bodies stay whole. The script must not contain BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK/SAVEPOINT (the verb owns the transaction); commands the server refuses inside a transaction block (VACUUM, CREATE DATABASE) belong in run_statement with autocommit=true. Each statement reports its command tag and row count; rows are never returned (use run_query). Vendor GRANTs alone decide what runs. Returns a queued job.
embedding_description: Apply a multi-statement SQL script or schema migration to an external Postgres database as one atomic transaction with a savepoint per statement. Roll everything back at the first failure, naming the failing statement, or skip failures and commit the rest, or dry-run and roll back. Reports each statement's command tag and row count.

result_processor_customizations.result_description: Dispatch envelope: job_id (string) and status ('queued'). The script's outcome arrives when the job completes: {statement_count, succeeded_count, failed_count, committed, on_error, statements: [{index, command, status, command_tag, rowcount, has_result_set} or {index, command, status: failed, error_code, sqlstate, message}]}.
result_processor_customizations.presentation_guidance: This call only confirms the job was queued; do not say the script ran. Once delivered, report whether it committed, how many statements succeeded and failed, and name each failed statement by its number and message. A rollback-mode failure arrives as an error naming the statement; nothing from that script was committed.

error_processor_customizations.action_context: Run a multi-statement SQL script in one transaction against a registered foreign Postgres connection.
error_processor_customizations.error_interpretation: external_pg.script_statement_failed: one statement failed in on_error=rollback mode; the message names its number, keyword, text, the classified error code and SQLSTATE, and the whole script was rolled back. external_pg.invalid_params: missing connection_name or sql, an empty script, an on_error other than rollback/continue, a non-boolean commit, or a transaction-control statement (BEGIN, COMMIT, ROLLBACK, SAVEPOINT, RELEASE, PREPARE TRANSACTION) in the script. external_pg.connection_unknown: no connection registered under that name. external_pg.auth_failed: the registered credential was rejected. external_pg.platform_db_refused: the connection targets the platform's own database.
error_processor_customizations.recovery_guidance: external_pg.script_statement_failed: fix the named statement and rerun the whole script (nothing was committed), or rerun with on_error=continue to keep the statements that succeed. SQLSTATE 25001 in the message means that statement cannot run inside a transaction block: run it alone through run_statement with autocommit=true. external_pg.invalid_params naming transaction control: remove BEGIN/COMMIT/SAVEPOINT; the verb owns the transaction. external_pg.connection_unknown: run list_connections.
